Date of Service: September 13, 2026, September 27, 2026, October 11, 2026  

Dear Appeals Coordinator,

I am writing to formally request an internal appeal of the denial for claim number 2026-PA-118734, dated October 26, 2026, which stated: "This claim has been denied because prior authorization was not obtained before the services were provided, as required for specialty infusion medications."

Under Section 5.2 Prior Authorization of the Cascade Community Health Plan policy, retrospective authorization will be granted when the service would have been approved had prior authorization been requested and the provider submits documentation within 90 days of the date of service. The Infusion Center Note dated September 8, 2026 confirms that a prior authorization request was faxed to Cascade on September 8, 2026 (confirmation #F-882173), five days before the September 13, 2026 infusion, with no response received prior to service. This timely submission satisfies the policy’s requirement for retrospective review, as the request was made well within the 90-day window and prior to the service date.

Furthermore, Section 5.3 Continuity of Care provides that members receiving an ongoing course of treatment under a previous health plan at the time of enrollment may continue that treatment for up to 90 days while prior authorization is obtained. The Gastroenterology Note from Dr. Helen Park dated September 6, 2026 states that the patient had been on infliximab 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks since 2023 under Evergreen Health, with sustained remission, and that Cascade Community Health Plan became effective August 13, 2026. This confirms ongoing therapy at the time of plan change, qualifying the patient for continuity of care protection during the authorization process.

Additionally, Section 6.1 Crohn's Disease Biologic Therapy specifies that infliximab is covered for moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease after an inadequate response to, or intolerance of, at least one conventional therapy. The same gastroenterology note documents failure of azathioprine from 2020 to 2022 due to hepatotoxicity and confirms continued infliximab use since 2023 with sustained remission, establishing medical necessity under the plan’s coverage criteria.

Given the patient’s stable three-year history on infliximab and the high risk of flare and antibody formation associated with interruption—as noted in the September 6, 2026 gastroenterology record—I request an expedited appeal under Section 10.1 Appeals, which allows for a decision within 72 hours when the standard timeframe could seriously jeopardize the member's health.

I respectfully request that Cascade Community Health Plan overturn the denial, authorize and pay for the infliximab infusions administered on September 13, 2026, September 27, 2026, and October 11, 2026, and provide a peer-to-peer review upon request. Please also provide a full copy of the claim file and the clinical criteria used in the original denial determination.

Enclosures:  
Copy of the prior authorization request fax confirmation (#F-882173) sent to Cascade on September 8, 2026  
Medical records showing continuous infliximab use since 2023 and failure of azathioprine
